bullets.text: Working title (per analyst): "Determinants of Hospital HCAHPS Star Ratings and Changes Over Time, 2017-2024".
bullets.rationale: The title fixes the artifact's scope and is non-negotiable per the analyst.

bullets.text: HCAHPS = Hospital Consumer Assessment of Healthcare Providers and Systems — spell out in the title or at first use in the abstract.
bullets.rationale: Acronym expansion the reader needs, but a drafting instruction rather than argument content.

bullets.text: Objectives (~30 words): state the question — what hospital, operational, and community factors are associated with the overall HCAHPS star rating, and which explain the 2017-2024 change.
bullets.rationale: States the research question; the abstract cannot stand without it.

bullets.text: Methods (~45 words): U.S. acute-care hospitals reporting HCAHPS in Q1 2017 and the latest 2024 release wave (N approximately 2,380); ordinary least squares regression...
bullets.rationale: Defines the sample and design a reader needs to judge the result.

bullets.text: Results (~70 words): mean rating fell 3.45 to 3.27 stars; the factor set explained about a quarter of the variation in both years but only 4%-6% of the change...
bullets.rationale: Carries the headline finding that answers the question.

bullets.text: Conclusions (~35 words): observable factors account for where ratings stand but little of how they move — payment-linked ratings reflect community context...
bullets.rationale: States the dual-policy message the paper is built to deliver.

bullets.text: Note: abstract Results state magnitude and direction in plain language; no R-squared symbol, no "coefficient." Translate consistently with the Results section.
bullets.rationale: Drafting instruction that aids readability but is not abstract content itself.

bullets.text: Topic sentence: hospital patient experience, measured by the HCAHPS survey, is publicly reported and tied to Medicare payment, so HCAHPS scores carry financial and reputational stakes.
bullets.rationale: Topic sentence establishing why HCAHPS scores matter — the premise of the whole paper.

bullets.text: HCAHPS is the standardized national survey of inpatient experience; CMS publishes overall star ratings on Care Compare.
bullets.rationale: Background that situates HCAHPS but the argument survives without the definitional detail.

bullets.text: Scores feed the Hospital Value-Based Purchasing program, so a rating gain or loss moves Medicare reimbursement.
bullets.rationale: The payment link is the stake the entire policy framing rests on.

bullets.text: One sentence on why ratings as a payment signal are worth scrutinizing — measurement choices and survey trends shape the incentive.
bullets.rationale: Enrichment; the payment-stakes point is already made by the surrounding bullets.

bullets.text: Transition: because ratings drive payment, what they actually capture about a hospital matters.
bullets.rationale: Bridge bullet carrying the move into the literature paragraph.

bullets.text: Topic sentence: research on HCAHPS scores splits into two strands — studies of what predicts ratings at a point in time, and studies of how ratings moved nationally during the pandemic.
bullets.rationale: Frames the prior-work structure the gap statement builds on.

bullets.text: Cross-sectional work links ratings to hospital characteristics, nursing, and county community factors.
bullets.rationale: One of the two strands the gap statement is defined against.

bullets.text: A separate strand documents the national decline in patient experience during the pandemic and its persistence afterward — kept brief, as background.
bullets.rationale: The second strand the gap statement contrasts against; without it the gap has no second pole.

bullets.text: Pre-pandemic trend work establishes the flat-to-improving baseline the post-2017 decline reverses.
bullets.rationale: Adds context for the baseline year choice but the gap stands without it.

bullets.text: A third, methodological strand examines how the rating is built and adjusted — CMS patient-mix adjustment and peer grouping — motivating cautious interpretation.
bullets.rationale: Methodology-critique strand is out of scope per CLAUDE.md; cuttable under word pressure.

bullets.text: Transition: these strands describe ratings at one time or trace a national average, but they leave one question open.
bullets.rationale: Bridge bullet setting up the gap paragraph.

bullets.text: Topic sentence: no study has modeled, at the hospital level, both where overall star ratings stand and how individual hospitals' ratings changed... using the same factors.
bullets.rationale: The gap statement; the paper's reason for existing.

bullets.text: Cross-sectional determinant studies describe levels at one time but cannot say whether the same factors explain movement.
bullets.rationale: Substantiates one half of the gap but the gap sentence already states it.

bullets.text: National-trend studies trace the average trajectory but do not decompose hospital-level change against hospital and community factors.
bullets.rationale: Substantiates the other half of the gap but the gap sentence already states it.

bullets.text: Why the distinction matters: if factors explain where ratings stand but not how they move, the policy reading of a rating change differs from the reading of a rating level.
bullets.rationale: Justifies why the gap is worth filling — the link from gap to policy payoff.

bullets.text: Transition: this study addresses that gap directly.
bullets.rationale: Bridge bullet into the objective paragraph.

bullets.text: Topic sentence: we examined which hospital, operational, and county community factors are associated with the overall HCAHPS star rating, and which explain the 2017-2024 change.
bullets.rationale: States the study objective; the reader cannot follow the paper without it.

bullets.text: Design in one sentence: a hospital-level analysis comparing Q1 2017 with the latest 2024 release wave, modeling rating levels in each year and the change between them.
bullets.rationale: The one-sentence design preview the reader needs before Methods.

bullets.text: State the framing is associational and decomposition-based — compares how much variation factors explain across level and change models, makes no causal claim.
bullets.rationale: Sets the inferential ceiling; without it readers may over-read the findings.

bullets.text: No findings preview (AJPH convention).
bullets.rationale: Drafting instruction enforcing journal convention, not argument content.

bullets.text: Topic sentence (describes): we built a dataset with two snapshots per hospital — Q1 2017 and the latest 2024 release — combining patient-experience ratings with operational, market, community-health, demographic, and geographic measures.
bullets.rationale: Topic sentence defining the two-snapshot design that makes the levels-vs-change contrast possible.

bullets.text: Outcome and ratings source: overall HCAHPS star rating and sub-domain ratings from the CMS Care Compare longitudinal HCAHPS file, 23 quarterly release waves.
bullets.rationale: Identifies the outcome variable and its source — essential for trusting the result.

bullets.text: Hospital characteristics from CMS Hospital General Information; ED throughput from the CMS Timely and Effective Care file, 2017 and 2024 vintages.
bullets.rationale: Data provenance for key factors; informs interpretation but the design holds without naming each file.

bullets.text: County context: poor health from CDC PLACES; hospital counts from CMS Provider of Services; demographics from ACS via IPUMS NHGIS; rural-urban from USDA RUCA codes; nurse salary and beds from CMS HCRIS.
bullets.rationale: Data-source enumeration; needed for reproducibility but not load-bearing for the argument.

bullets.text: Transition: these sources were merged into one row per hospital.
bullets.rationale: Bridge bullet to the sample-construction paragraph.

bullets.text: Topic sentence (describes): the analytic sample comprised U.S. acute-care hospitals reporting an overall HCAHPS star rating in both the Q1 2017 and latest 2024 release waves, with complete data.
bullets.rationale: Defines the analytic sample; the reader cannot judge generalizability without it.

bullets.text: Linkage: hospitals matched to county context through ZIP code and a ZIP-to-county crosswalk; community measures merged on county FIPS code.
bullets.rationale: Linkage method informs interpretation of the county measures but does not determine the finding.

bullets.text: Complete-case rule: a hospital entered only if it had no missing values on the outcome or any factor in either year; the resulting sample is N approximately 2,380.
bullets.rationale: STROBE missing-data element and the sample size — both essential and reporting-guideline protected.

bullets.text: STROBE item — report exclusions: tabulate hospitals dropped and the reason so the sample can be reconstructed; consider a flow diagram.
bullets.rationale: STROBE reporting-guideline element; preserved, but informs interpretation rather than driving the argument.

bullets.text: Caveat: the descriptive maps assign each ZIP to up to four counties, while the regression sample assigns each hospital to one county — note the two conventions.
bullets.rationale: Methodological caveat that informs how the maps are read; not load-bearing for the regression finding.

bullets.text: Topic sentence (describes): the outcome was the overall HCAHPS star rating (1-5 stars); sub-domain ratings were used only as additional factors in some models, never as the outcome.
bullets.rationale: Pins down the dependent variable and a scope boundary the reader must have.

bullets.text: Hospital factors: ownership recoded into three classes; rural-urban classification in three classes (urban, large rural/micropolitan, small or isolated rural).
bullets.rationale: Defines the ownership and rurality factors central to the cross-sectional findings.

bullets.text: Operational and market factors: median ED time in minutes; hospitals per 1,000 county population.
bullets.rationale: Defines ED time, the operational factor that carries the agency half of the headline.

bullets.text: County community factors: self-reported poor health prevalence; population; share aged 65+; race and ethnicity shares; foreign-born share; education; poverty; median household income.
bullets.rationale: Enumerates the community factors; the set matters but individual list items do not each determine the finding.

bullets.text: Caveat: the share-Hispanic measure was built from the Asian-population count rather than the Hispanic count — a likely coding error; estimates may shift.
bullets.rationale: Data-quality caveat that affects one factor's estimates but not the central asymmetry.

bullets.text: Caveat: median ED time fell 111 minutes (38%) between 2017 and 2024 vintages; part may reflect a CMS measure-definition change, which affects how the ED finding is read.
bullets.rationale: Determines whether the ED finding — the agency half of the headline — can be trusted.

bullets.text: Topic sentence (describes): for the change analysis, each factor had a matching 2017-2024 change measure, computed as the 2024 value minus the 2017 value.
bullets.rationale: Defines the change-score construction underlying the paper's central contrast.

bullets.text: The outcome change measure was the 2024 overall star rating minus the 2017 rating.
bullets.rationale: Defines the dependent variable of the change model — the paper's headline outcome.

bullets.text: Ownership and rural-urban classification were treated as fixed over the window and entered the change model as categorical factors.
bullets.rationale: Modeling choice that informs interpretation of the rural and ownership change results.

bullets.text: Transition: these change measures fed the change model described next.
bullets.rationale: Minimal transition; adjacent topic sentences already carry the connection.

bullets.text: Topic sentence (describes): we estimated the overall star rating with OLS and heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors, fitting three linked models — 2017 levels, 2024 levels, and the 2017-2024 change.
bullets.rationale: States the core estimation approach the entire Results section rests on.

bullets.text: The level models regressed the rating on that year's factors; the change model regressed the change in rating on the changes in those factors.
bullets.rationale: Specifies the three models whose contrast is the paper's central finding.

bullets.text: Augmented models added the sub-domain star ratings and 2017 baseline values, testing whether those channels close the gap between level and change models.
bullets.rationale: Secondary models that inform but do not determine the headline asymmetry.

bullets.text: The central comparison: the share of variation explained by the level models versus the change model — reported as a percentage, stated consistently.
bullets.rationale: Names the explicit quantitative contrast that is the paper's contribution.

bullets.text: Subgroup analysis: the change model re-estimated separately for urban, large rural, and small rural hospitals.
bullets.rationale: Supports a secondary descriptive finding; the headline holds without it.

bullets.text: Sensitivity analysis: nurse salary per bed added to the level and change models as a staffing-intensity check.
bullets.rationale: Robustness check that strengthens but does not establish the main result.

bullets.text: Caveat: sub-domain, subgroup, and nurse-per-bed estimates live outside the repository; coefficients must be retrieved before drafting the corresponding Results paragraphs.
bullets.rationale: Drafting flag the writer must act on; affects secondary paragraphs, not the headline.

bullets.text: Ethics: analysis used public, de-identified, hospital-level data; state whether IRB review was required or exempt. [TBD]
bullets.rationale: TBD-only; cannot grade until the IRB status is resolved.

bullets.text: Topic sentence: the 2,380 hospitals spanned ownership types and rural-urban settings, and several factors shifted between 2017 and 2024.
bullets.rationale: Topic sentence orienting the reader to the sample and to Table 1.

bullets.text: Composition: 66.5% for-profit, 18.7% non-profit, 14.8% government; 69.5% urban, 20.8% large rural, 9.7% small or isolated rural.
bullets.rationale: Descriptive composition that contextualizes the sample but is not load-bearing for the finding.

bullets.text: Headline shifts: mean overall rating fell 3.45 to 3.27 stars; median ED time fell 292 to 181 minutes.
bullets.rationale: The national decline and ED-time drop are the aggregate facts the change analysis explains.

bullets.text: Caveat: mean share White fell about 11 points and median household income rose about $12,800 — both larger than typical and possibly tabulation artifacts; verify before stating as population change.
bullets.rationale: Data-quality caveat affecting how two descriptive shifts are reported, not the central finding.

bullets.text: Transition: these are the aggregate shifts; the regressions show what is associated with the rating itself.
bullets.rationale: Bridge bullet moving from descriptives to the regression results.

bullets.text: Topic sentence: in both 2017 and 2024, the factors together explained about a quarter of the variation in overall star ratings across hospitals, and the associations were stable.
bullets.rationale: Reports the cross-sectional explained-variation figure — one pole of the central contrast.

bullets.text: State the explained-variation figure in plain language and use the same phrasing in the abstract and Discussion.
bullets.rationale: Phrasing-consistency instruction with no argument content; logic chain fully intact without it.

bullets.text: Stability across years is itself a finding — the structure under the national decline held steady.
bullets.rationale: Secondary finding that adds nuance; the central asymmetry survives without emphasizing stability.

bullets.text: Transition: within that stable structure, three patterns stand out.
bullets.rationale: Bridge bullet into the cross-sectional pattern paragraphs.

bullets.text: Topic sentence: government hospitals scored highest and non-profit lowest, and small rural hospitals scored well above urban hospitals.
bullets.rationale: Topic sentence reporting the ownership and rural patterns the policy discussion uses.

bullets.text: Non-profit hospitals scored roughly half a star below government in both years; for-profit matched government in 2017 but moved about 0.11 stars below by 2024.
bullets.rationale: Quantifies the ownership pattern; adds depth but the headline does not turn on the magnitudes.

bullets.text: Small rural hospitals scored above urban in both years and the gap widened (0.32 to 0.61 stars); large rural trailed urban in 2017 but caught up.
bullets.rationale: Quantifies the rural pattern, a supporting finding under the change story.

bullets.text: Note the rural pattern runs opposite to the rural disadvantage seen on most non-experience quality measures.
bullets.rationale: Interesting contrast but cuttable; the rural finding is supporting, not headline.

bullets.text: Transition: operational and community factors pointed in expected directions, with one exception.
bullets.rationale: Bridge bullet that also flags the counterintuitive result coming next.

bullets.text: Topic sentence: longer ED time and a more disadvantaged community were associated with lower ratings, except that higher self-reported poor health was associated with higher ratings.
bullets.rationale: Topic sentence reporting the operational and community associations, including the counterintuitive sign.

bullets.text: Each additional minute of ED time was associated with a slightly lower rating; more hospitals per 1,000 population was associated with higher ratings.
bullets.rationale: The ED-time level association underpins the agency argument in the Discussion.

bullets.text: Higher county education was associated with higher ratings; higher shares aged 65+, foreign-born, and in poverty (2024) were associated with lower ratings.
bullets.rationale: Detail on community associations that supports the levels-side policy argument.

bullets.text: The counterintuitive result: higher county self-reported poor health was associated with higher ratings in both years — flagged here, addressed in the Discussion.
bullets.rationale: Sets up the poor-health finding that an entire Discussion paragraph is built to interpret.

bullets.text: Transition: the level models explain a quarter of the variation; the change model explains far less.
bullets.rationale: Bridge bullet that states the levels-vs-change asymmetry as it pivots to the change results.

bullets.text: Topic sentence: the same factor set that explained a quarter of the variation in levels explained only 4%-6% of the variation in the 2017-2024 change — an order of magnitude less.
bullets.rationale: States the levels-vs-change asymmetry, the paper's central quantitative finding.

bullets.text: Report both change figures: about 4% basic, about 6% with 2017 baseline values; the gap is consistent with regression toward the mean.
bullets.rationale: Supplies the only account of why the 4% and 6% figures differ; without it the change R² reads as unexplained noise.

bullets.text: This asymmetry — factors explain where ratings stand but little of how they move — is the central quantitative finding.
bullets.rationale: Names the contribution explicitly; the reader must register it as the headline.

bullets.text: Transition: within that small explained share, the change model still identifies a few factors.
bullets.rationale: Bridge bullet into the change-predictor paragraph.

bullets.text: Topic sentence: among the factors in the change model, shorter ED time was the operational factor associated with rating gains, while community shifts were unrelated to rating change.
bullets.rationale: Topic sentence reporting both halves of the change finding the Discussion builds on.

bullets.text: ED time: a reduction was associated with a small rating gain; given the 111-minute mean drop, the implied average gain was roughly 0.1-0.2 stars.
bullets.rationale: The ED-change result is the operational lever the agency argument depends on.

bullets.text: Community shifts: changes in age, race, foreign-born share, education, and poverty were all unrelated to rating change — the population-shift story does not explain the rating-shift story.
bullets.rationale: The null on community change is half the asymmetry and underpins the caution against attributing the decline.

bullets.text: Supporting (descriptive): rural hospitals gained relative to urban (large rural +0.20, small rural +0.28); for-profit and non-profit declined more than government.
bullets.rationale: Descriptive supporting findings under the change story, explicitly not the headline.

bullets.text: Caveat: rural-subgroup change estimates rest on files outside the repository and need retrieval before this paragraph is drafted in full.
bullets.rationale: Drafting flag affecting a supporting paragraph; the writer must act on it.

bullets.text: Geographic pattern: describe the 2017-2024 difference map — which regions improved, which declined — once the rendered figure is available.
bullets.rationale: Adds geographic texture tied to Figure 1; the change argument holds without the regional detail.

bullets.text: Topic sentence: factors explained about a quarter of where ratings stood but only 4%-6% of how they changed between 2017 and 2024.
bullets.rationale: Restates the central finding as the Discussion's opening principal-findings claim.

bullets.text: Restate the asymmetry plainly and note the cross-sectional structure held steady across the two years.
bullets.rationale: Topic sentence already states the asymmetry; the stability point is minor and redundant with results-p11-3, so the central argument is intact without it.

bullets.text: Name the one operational factor that did track rating change — ED time — and note community shifts did not.
bullets.rationale: Carries the ED-time finding into the Discussion, where the agency argument needs it.

bullets.text: Transition: this pattern fits and extends what prior work has shown.
bullets.rationale: Bridge bullet into the literature-comparison paragraph.

bullets.text: Topic sentence: the cross-sectional associations align with existing determinant studies, and the change finding extends the national-trend literature.
bullets.rationale: Topic sentence positioning the contribution against prior work.

bullets.text: Level findings echo prior work on community factors and hospital characteristics.
bullets.rationale: Situates the level findings in the literature; adds credibility but is not load-bearing.

bullets.text: The national decline matches the documented pandemic-era trajectory; this paper adds that observable factors explain little of the hospital-level variation in that change.
bullets.rationale: States precisely how the change finding extends the literature — the contribution claim.

bullets.text: The rural advantage is consistent with recent work showing rural and critical access hospitals outperform on patient experience.
bullets.rationale: Situates a supporting finding; cuttable under word pressure with no harm to the headline.

bullets.text: Transition: the asymmetry carries a paired policy message.
bullets.rationale: Bridge bullet into the two policy-implication paragraphs.

bullets.text: Topic sentence: because a quarter of the variation in levels tracks community factors hospitals cannot change, payment-linked ratings disadvantage hospitals serving disadvantaged communities.
bullets.rationale: States the levels-side policy implication — half the dual-policy headline.

bullets.text: CMS patient-mix adjustment corrects for individual patient characteristics but not community context, so this disadvantage survives current adjustment.
bullets.rationale: The mechanism that makes the levels-side critique policy-relevant rather than abstract.

bullets.text: The National Academies set out the rationale for adjusting quality measures for social risk; these results give updated, HCAHPS-specific support.
bullets.rationale: Anchors the recommendation in an authoritative report; strengthens but does not establish it.

bullets.text: Implication: CMS should consider community-context adjusters or context-adjusted scores alongside raw stars — the "bad news for incentive programs" half.
bullets.rationale: The actionable recommendation that completes the levels-side policy message.

bullets.text: Transition: the change side of the asymmetry carries the opposite message.
bullets.rationale: Bridge bullet pivoting to the agency-side implication paragraph.

bullets.text: Topic sentence: because the variation factors explain in change runs through ED throughput, hospitals retain real, if narrow, agency over their rating trajectory.
bullets.rationale: States the agency-side policy implication — the other half of the dual-policy headline.

bullets.text: Scope this agency claim narrowly to operations (ED throughput); ownership and rural-urban differences are descriptive, not part of the agency claim (resolved framing decision).
bullets.rationale: Bounds the headline claim per a resolved framing decision; mis-scoping would overclaim.

bullets.text: The ED-throughput-to-satisfaction link is supported by the wait-time literature.
bullets.rationale: Literature support for the ED mechanism; strengthens but does not establish the agency claim.

bullets.text: Implication: the operational room to improve a rating is narrower than the cross-sectional picture suggests, but it is real — the "good news for hospital management" half.
bullets.rationale: The actionable takeaway that completes the agency-side policy message.

bullets.text: Supporting context (descriptive): rural hospitals gained ground even amid rural-hospital financial fragility; for-profit and non-profit declined more than government.
bullets.rationale: Descriptive enrichment explicitly outside the agency claim; cuttable under word pressure.

bullets.text: Transition: one finding still needs explanation.
bullets.rationale: Bridge bullet into the counterintuitive-sign paragraph.

bullets.text: Topic sentence: the positive association between county self-reported poor health and ratings runs against expectation and should be read cautiously.
bullets.rationale: Topic sentence addressing a counterintuitive finding the reader will otherwise stumble on.

bullets.text: Offer candidate explanations — community-care engagement and survey participation, or collider-style confounding — without overclaiming.
bullets.rationale: Adds interpretive depth; the caution stands even if the candidate explanations are trimmed.

bullets.text: Broader caution: because structural factors do not drive rating change, a rating shift is not a reliable signal of community-driven structural change.
bullets.rationale: Draws the key inferential limit from the asymmetry; central to honest interpretation.

bullets.text: Transition: these readings hold within the study's limits.
bullets.rationale: Bridge bullet into the limitations paragraph.

bullets.text: Topic sentence: several limitations bound the interpretation.
bullets.rationale: Topic sentence opening a required limitations paragraph.

bullets.text: Design: associational and decomposition-based — no causal claim; the change model nets out time-invariant traits but cannot identify mechanisms.
bullets.rationale: The central limitation that bounds every causal reading of the findings.

bullets.text: Measurement: the ED-time measure definition may have changed between vintages, so the 111-minute drop may overstate real operational gain.
bullets.rationale: Directly qualifies the ED finding that carries the agency half of the headline.

bullets.text: Data error: the share-Hispanic measure was built from the Asian-population count; estimates involving it may shift once corrected.
bullets.rationale: Important caveat affecting one factor, but the central asymmetry does not depend on it.

bullets.text: Scope: only the overall star rating is the outcome; intra-pandemic dynamics, hospital fixed effects, and a Star Ratings critique are out of scope.
bullets.rationale: Defines scope boundaries; useful for the reader but does not change the interpretation.

bullets.text: Geography: descriptive maps and regressions use different ZIP-to-county conventions.
bullets.rationale: Minor methodological caveat that does not change practical interpretation of the regressions.

bullets.text: Unverified estimates: sub-domain, subgroup, and nurse-per-bed results were not yet retrievable from repository files at outlining time.
bullets.rationale: An outlining-stage process note that should resolve before drafting, not a durable limitation.

bullets.text: Topic sentence: observable factors explain where ratings stand far better than how they move, and that asymmetry should shape how ratings are used.
bullets.rationale: The closing statement of the central finding and its significance.

bullets.text: For payment policy: pair raw stars with community-context adjustment so hospitals are not penalized for the populations they serve.
bullets.rationale: Restates the levels-side recommendation as a closing takeaway.

bullets.text: For hospital management: trajectory remains partly within reach through operational improvement, most visibly ED throughput.
bullets.rationale: Restates the agency-side recommendation as a closing takeaway.

bullets.text: Close on the paired message without overclaiming either half.
bullets.rationale: Drafting instruction on tone; the two takeaway bullets already deliver the message.

bullets.text: Table 1 — Descriptive statistics: hospital, operational, and community factors, 2017 and 2024 snapshots, with the change.
bullets.rationale: Descriptive exhibit that contextualizes the sample but does not carry the headline.

bullets.text: Table 2 — Regression results, four columns: 2024 levels, 2017 levels, change (basic), change (with 2017 baselines).
bullets.rationale: The exhibit that displays the levels-vs-change contrast central to the paper.

bullets.text: Figure 1 — County map of the 2017-2024 change in mean overall star rating.
bullets.rationale: Adds geographic texture; the change argument holds on Table 2 alone.

bullets.text: Appendix — Per-year county star-rating maps (eight release waves, 2017-2024).
bullets.rationale: Supplementary maps; cuttable with no harm to the main argument.
